title: Your Baby Has 10 Seconds Left

style: Cinematic photorealistic film still, vertical 9:16 composition with the subject centered, shallow depth of field, moody cinematic sci-fi color grade with red accents, present day, no readable text or numbers unless described.

scenes.image: Vertical close-up of a terrified father holding a three-week-old newborn baby girl in a pink-and-blue striped knit hat and a striped hospital-style blanket, an empty glowing red hologram frame floating above the baby with no digits, dark hospital-like room with red light.
lines: [intense] You wake up. And there's a number floating above your baby's head.

scenes.image: Close-up of a three-week-old newborn baby girl in a pink-and-blue striped knit hat and a striped hospital-style blanket sleeping, red glow above her.
Emma in a kitchen doorway at dawn, hand over mouth, red light on her face.
Daniel and Emma staring at each other in a dim room, a soft pale blue glow above each of their heads, no readable digits.
lines: Above your head: sixty-three years. Above your wife's: forty-two. Above your three-week-old daughter... five seconds.

scenes.image: Daniel clutching the baby, shouting toward Emma holding a phone.
Daniel pressing his forehead against a three-week-old newborn baby girl in a pink-and-blue striped knit hat and a striped hospital-style blanket, eyes shut, tears.
lines: [breaking] Please. I'm right here. I'm not going anywhere.

scenes.image: Macro close-up of a three-week-old newborn baby girl in a pink-and-blue striped knit hat and a striped hospital-style blanket's face in red light.
a three-week-old newborn baby girl in a pink-and-blue striped knit hat and a striped hospital-style blanket smiling up in warm light, red glow gone.
lines: She smiles. She's alive. And the number is gone.
scenes.motion: The newborn blinks and breaks into a tiny smile, warm light, slow push-in.

scenes.image: A smartphone exploding with notifications on a dresser.
lines: Then his phone explodes. Every human on Earth just woke up with a countdown. And it isn't counting what everyone thinks.
